description: Hi! I’m Yavuz, a 5th grade student in Türkiye, and I’m really curious about space, planets and stars, especially [Mars / the Moon / black holes / rockets]. I enjoy coming up with creative ideas, [drawing / building with Lego / making simple games in Scratch], and I like working in a team and learning new things quickly. If you join my team, you’ll get an energetic, curious teammate who loves sharing ideas and can help with storytelling and presenting our project.
summary: Our project is stories of space machines we left behind. We give some interesting and real informations. We tell stories about space machines. What are they do now? What are they used for now? Or what we learn someting abot that space machines? You can learn answers of thees questions.
details: Our project is a storytelling presentation called “Abandoned But Not Forgotten.” It tells kids about machines that NASA left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Machines can’t talk, so we gave them a voice! Four machines introduce themselves in speech bubbles and tell their own stories: the Moon Mirror from Apollo 11, Oppy the Mars rover, Ginny the Mars helicopter and Voyager 1. We turned big numbers into simple comparisons. For example, the Moon moves away from Earth about as much as your fingernails grow in a year. Every slide is in both English and Turkish, so more children can understand it. We want kids to see these machines as space heroes, not space junk, and to get curious about science. We researched NASA websites and news articles. We made the slides and drawings with an online slide tool, and an AI assistant (Claude) helped us with research and design. We thought about our audience a lot: short sentences, friendly characters, bright colors and a question for the audience at the end.
